# Semantic Retrieval Benchmark Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build an evaluation suite that can actually distinguish one embedding model from another, and a runner that compares every preset on it.

**Architecture:** A new tiered suite of short keyword queries against short factual atoms, generated by a script that enforces the overlap rule per tier. The eval command gains per-tier metric breakdown. A comparison runner sweeps every preset through download, reindex, evaluate and teardown, printing one table.

**Tech Stack:** Node ESM scripts (`.mjs`), the existing `knowl eval retrieval` command, vitest.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/embedding-model-selection.md`, "Benchmark" section.

**Depends on:** Tasks 1-5 of `2026-08-02-embedding-model-selection.md` for the multi-preset runner in Task 3. Tasks 1 and 2 of this plan stand alone and can be built and run against the current model today.

## Global Constraints

- Branch: `feat/embedding-model-selection`. Do not commit to `main`.
- Test command: `npm.cmd test`. Generator run: `node scripts/generate-semantic-suite.mjs`.
- The existing suites in `docs/evals/` are **not** modified. They remain valid regression checks.
- Suite shape matches the existing files: `{ version, description, fixtures, cases }`.
- Fixture ids are unique; the generator throws on a duplicate, as the existing one does.
- Queries are 2-6 words, matching what `KNOWL.md` tells agents to send.
- Tier mix: about 65% basic, 25% moderate, 10% extreme, total 100-120 cases.
- Extreme-tier cases must have **zero** content-word overlap with their expected item, enforced by the generator.
- No network access in tests.

### Task 1: The tiered suite and its generator

**Files:**
- Create: `scripts/generate-semantic-suite.mjs`
- Create: `docs/evals/semantic-suite.json` (generated output, committed)
- Create: `tests/benchmark/semantic-suite.test.ts`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `docs/evals/semantic-suite.json` with shape
  `{ version: 1, description: string, fixtures: Fixture[], cases: Case[] }`
  where `Fixture = { id, category, title, content, tags?, status?, lang? }`
  and `Case = { id, tier: 'basic'|'moderate'|'extreme', query, expectedItemIds, mustNotReturn, limit }`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Create `tests/benchmark/semantic-suite.test.ts`:

```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const suite = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.resolve('docs/evals/semantic-suite.json'), 'utf8'));

const STOPWORDS = new Set([
  'the', 'a', 'an', 'of', 'to', 'in', 'is', 'are', 'was', 'were', 'and', 'or', 'for', 'on', 'at',
  'by', 'we', 'our', 'do', 'does', 'did', 'what', 'why', 'how', 'when', 'which', 'that', 'this',
  'it', 'be', 'with', 'as', 'from', 'have', 'has', 'can', 'should', 'not', 'no', 'use', 'used', 'uses',
]);

function contentWords(text: string): string[] {
  const words = String(text).toLowerCase().match(/[a-z0-9]+/g) ?? [];
  return [...new Set(words)].filter(word => !STOPWORDS.has(word) && word.length > 2);
}

const fixtures = new Map<string, any>(suite.fixtures.map((f: any) => [f.id, f]));

function fixtureText(id: string): string {
  const fixture = fixtures.get(id);
  return `${fixture.title} ${fixture.content} ${(fixture.tags ?? []).join(' ')}`;
}

describe('semantic suite shape', () => {
  it('has 100 to 120 cases', () => {
    expect(suite.cases.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(100);
    expect(suite.cases.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(120);
  });

  it('gives every case a tier and a resolvable expected item', () => {
    for (const testCase of suite.cases) {
      expect(['basic', 'moderate', 'extreme']).toContain(testCase.tier);
      expect(testCase.expectedItemIds.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      for (const id of testCase.expectedItemIds) expect(fixtures.has(id)).toBe(true);
      for (const id of testCase.mustNotReturn) expect(fixtures.has(id)).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  it('keeps queries to the 2-6 keywords agents actually send', () => {
    for (const testCase of suite.cases) {
      const words = String(testCase.query).trim().split(/\s+/);
      expect(words.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
      expect(words.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(6);
    }
  });

  it('holds the intended tier mix', () => {
    const share = (tier: string) =>
      suite.cases.filter((c: any) => c.tier === tier).length / suite.cases.length;
    expect(share('basic')).toBeGreaterThan(0.55);
    expect(share('extreme')).toBeGreaterThan(0.05);
    expect(share('extreme')).toBeLessThan(0.16);
  });
});

describe('tier discipline', () => {
  it('gives extreme cases zero lexical overlap with their target', () => {
    for (const testCase of suite.cases.filter((c: any) => c.tier === 'extreme')) {
      const queryWords = contentWords(testCase.query);
      for (const id of testCase.expectedItemIds) {
        const target = new Set(contentWords(fixtureText(id)));
        const shared = queryWords.filter(word => target.has(word));
        expect(shared, `case ${testCase.id} shares "${shared.join(', ')}"`).toEqual([]);
      }
    }
  });

  it('gives every extreme case at least one lexical decoy', () => {
    for (const testCase of suite.cases.filter((c: any) => c.tier === 'extreme')) {
      expect(testCase.mustNotReturn.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      const queryWords = new Set(contentWords(testCase.query));
      const decoyShares = testCase.mustNotReturn.some((id: string) =>
        contentWords(fixtureText(id)).some(word => queryWords.has(word)));
      expect(decoyShares, `case ${testCase.id} has no word-sharing decoy`).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  it('includes lexical-is-correct controls so the suite cannot reward ignoring keywords', () => {
    const controls = suite.cases.filter((c: any) => {
      const queryWords = new Set(contentWords(c.query));
      return c.expectedItemIds.some((id: string) =>
        contentWords(fixtureText(id)).filter(word => queryWords.has(word)).length >= 2);
    });
    expect(controls.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(20);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the generator**

Create `scripts/generate-semantic-suite.mjs`. Structure it as: a `FIXTURES` array, a `CASES` array, then validation and write. Model the file layout on `scripts/generate-retrieval-suite.mjs`.

```javascript
import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const STOPWORDS = new Set([
  'the', 'a', 'an', 'of', 'to', 'in', 'is', 'are', 'was', 'were', 'and', 'or', 'for', 'on', 'at',
  'by', 'we', 'our', 'do', 'does', 'did', 'what', 'why', 'how', 'when', 'which', 'that', 'this',
  'it', 'be', 'with', 'as', 'from', 'have', 'has', 'can', 'should', 'not', 'no', 'use', 'used', 'uses',
]);

const contentWords = text => [...new Set(String(text).toLowerCase().match(/[a-z0-9]+/g) ?? [])]
  .filter(word => !STOPWORDS.has(word) && word.length > 2);

// Atoms shaped like real Knowl memory: one fact each, a couple of sentences,
// the kind of thing knowl_store actually receives.
const FIXTURES = [
  { id: 'soft-delete', category: 'architecture', title: 'Rows are flagged, never removed',
    content: 'Records carry a deleted_at timestamp. Nothing is physically dropped, so an accidental purge can be undone by clearing the flag.',
    tags: ['persistence', 'deletion'] },
  { id: 'hard-purge', category: 'decision', title: 'Nightly purge drops expired audit rows',
    content: 'Audit rows older than 400 days are permanently removed by the nightly job. This deletion is irreversible and intentionally so.',
    tags: ['audit', 'retention'] },
  { id: 'db-postgres', category: 'decision', title: 'PostgreSQL as the primary datastore',
    content: 'PostgreSQL 16 is the primary transactional datastore. Chosen for relational guarantees, JSONB and mature replication.',
    tags: ['database', 'persistence'] },
  // ... continue to roughly 45-55 fixtures.
];

const CASES = [
  // BASIC (~65%): everyday rewording, partial overlap is expected and fine.
  { id: 'db-basic', tier: 'basic', query: 'main database engine',
    expectedItemIds: ['db-postgres'], mustNotReturn: [], limit: 10 },

  // MODERATE (~25%): synonym substitution, little overlap.
  { id: 'soft-delete-moderate', tier: 'moderate', query: 'soft delete behaviour',
    expectedItemIds: ['soft-delete'], mustNotReturn: ['hard-purge'], limit: 10 },

  // EXTREME (~10%): zero overlap plus a decoy that shares words with the query.
  { id: 'soft-delete-extreme', tier: 'extreme', query: 'reversible removal mechanism',
    expectedItemIds: ['soft-delete'], mustNotReturn: ['hard-purge'], limit: 10 },
  // ... continue to 100-120 cases.
];

// --- validation ---

const byId = new Map();
for (const fixture of FIXTURES) {
  if (byId.has(fixture.id)) throw new Error(`duplicate fixture id: ${fixture.id}`);
  byId.set(fixture.id, fixture);
}

const fixtureText = id => {
  const fixture = byId.get(id);
  if (!fixture) throw new Error(`case references unknown fixture: ${id}`);
  return `${fixture.title} ${fixture.content} ${(fixture.tags ?? []).join(' ')}`;
};

const seenCases = new Set();
for (const testCase of CASES) {
  if (seenCases.has(testCase.id)) throw new Error(`duplicate case id: ${testCase.id}`);
  seenCases.add(testCase.id);

  const words = testCase.query.trim().split(/\s+/);
  if (words.length < 2 || words.length > 6) {
    throw new Error(`case ${testCase.id}: query must be 2-6 words, got ${words.length}`);
  }

  for (const id of [...testCase.expectedItemIds, ...testCase.mustNotReturn]) fixtureText(id);

  // The rule that makes the extreme tier mean anything. Without it a case can
  // drift into being solvable by keyword match and the tier stops discriminating.
  if (testCase.tier === 'extreme') {
    const queryWords = contentWords(testCase.query);
    for (const id of testCase.expectedItemIds) {
      const target = new Set(contentWords(fixtureText(id)));
      const shared = queryWords.filter(word => target.has(word));
      if (shared.length > 0) {
        throw new Error(`extreme case ${testCase.id} shares "${shared.join(', ')}" with ${id}`);
      }
    }
    if (testCase.mustNotReturn.length === 0) {
      throw new Error(`extreme case ${testCase.id} needs at least one lexical decoy`);
    }
  }
}

const total = CASES.length;
if (total < 100 || total > 120) throw new Error(`expected 100-120 cases, got ${total}`);

const share = tier => CASES.filter(c => c.tier === tier).length / total;
if (share('basic') <= 0.55) throw new Error(`basic tier is ${(share('basic') * 100).toFixed(0)}%, expected >55%`);
if (share('extreme') <= 0.05 || share('extreme') >= 0.16) {
  throw new Error(`extreme tier is ${(share('extreme') * 100).toFixed(0)}%, expected 6-15%`);
}

const output = {
  version: 1,
  description:
    'Semantic retrieval suite. Tiered basic/moderate/extreme, weighted toward ordinary ' +
    'paraphrase because real stored atoms are ordinary. Extreme cases have zero content-word ' +
    'overlap with their target and carry a lexical decoy. Built to discriminate between ' +
    'embedding models, which the lexical retrieval-suite.json cannot.',
  fixtures: FIXTURES,
  cases: CASES,
};

writeFileSync(path.resolve('docs/evals/semantic-suite.json'), `${JSON.stringify(output, null, 2)}\n`, 'utf8');
console.log(`Wrote ${FIXTURES.length} fixtures and ${total} cases.`);
for (const tier of ['basic', 'moderate', 'extreme']) {
  console.log(`  ${tier}: ${CASES.filter(c => c.tier === tier).length}`);
}
```

Fill `FIXTURES` out to roughly 45-55 atoms and `CASES` to 100-120, honouring the tier mix. Draw subject matter from ordinary software-project memory: database choice, auth, caching, deployment, testing, observability, retention, rate limiting, feature flags, migrations. Pair each extreme case with a decoy fixture that genuinely shares a word with the query while meaning something else, as `hard-purge` does for `soft-delete`.

### Task 3: Preset comparison runner

Requires Tasks 1-5 of the model-selection plan.

**Files:**
- Create: `scripts/benchmark-embedding-models.mjs`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `knowl eval retrieval --dataset ... --vector --json`, the preset ids from `src/core/vector-profile.ts`, and `knowl config set search.vector.preset <id>`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the runner**

Create `scripts/benchmark-embedding-models.mjs`:

```javascript
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdtempSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';

const PRESETS = ['granite-small-en-r2', 'granite-97m-multilingual', 'bge-small-en', 'minilm-l6-en'];
const SUITE = path.resolve('docs/evals/semantic-suite.json');
const CLI = path.resolve('dist/index.js');

// A fresh store per preset. Sharing one would mean each run inherits the
// previous model's rows, and the fingerprint filter would silently hide them --
// producing a plausible table built on an empty corpus.
function runPreset(preset) {
  const root = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), `knowl-bench-${preset}-`));
  try {
    execFileSync('node', [CLI, 'init'], { cwd: root, stdio: 'inherit' });
    if (preset) execFileSync('node', [CLI, 'config', 'set', 'search.vector.preset', preset], { cwd: root, stdio: 'inherit' });

    const args = [CLI, 'eval', 'retrieval', '--dataset', SUITE, '--json'];
    if (preset) args.push('--vector');
    const output = execFileSync('node', args, { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8' });
    return JSON.parse(output);
  } finally {
    rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

const rows = [];
for (const preset of PRESETS) {
  console.error(`\n=== ${preset} ===`);
  rows.push({ label: preset, result: runPreset(preset) });
}
console.error('\n=== bm25 only (floor) ===');
rows.push({ label: 'bm25 only (floor)', result: runPreset(null) });

const tiers = ['basic', 'moderate', 'extreme'];
const header = ['model'.padEnd(26), ...tiers.map(t => t.padEnd(9)), 'overall'.padEnd(9), 'embed ms'];
console.log(`\n${header.join(' ')}`);

for (const row of rows) {
  const cells = tiers.map(tier => {
    const metrics = row.result.byTier?.[tier];
    return (metrics ? metrics.recallAt10.toFixed(4) : '-').padEnd(9);
  });
  console.log([
    row.label.padEnd(26),
    ...cells,
    String(row.result.recallAt10?.toFixed(4) ?? '-').padEnd(9),
    String(Math.round(row.result.averageLatencyMs ?? 0)),
  ].join(' '));
}

console.log('\nBasic is the deciding column: it predicts day-to-day quality.');
console.log('Extreme is a stress signal. A model that wins there while losing on basic is the wrong pick.');
console.log('If bm25-only matches the models across every tier, the suite is not discriminating.');
```

Adjust the JSON field names to match what `eval retrieval --json` actually emits — read that code path before finalising.

## Notes for the implementer

- **The suite's value is entirely in its construction.** If extreme cases leak lexical overlap, or the lexical-is-correct controls are dropped, it degenerates into the same instrument as `retrieval-suite.json` — which measures ranking regressions, not embedding quality.
- **A fresh store per preset is required** in Task 3. Sharing one lets the fingerprint filter hide the previous model's rows, producing a confident-looking table computed over nothing.
- **Report what the numbers say, not what we hoped.** The default was chosen on published scores from other corpora; this suite is the first measurement on Knowl-shaped content and is allowed to contradict them.
